tutorial.title: Quick guide
tutorial.indexLead: Pick a module to see what it does, what the form asks for, and where what you create shows up later.
tutorial.lead: What it is, what the form asks for, and where you use it later.

home.hook: The summary: balance, income, expenses and what's coming.
home.what: The summary panel. At the top, today's rate and four figures: Available (your real balance right now across every account), Income and Expenses for the period you pick, and Net, which is income minus expenses for that period.
home.form: No form here. The period filter (week, month, 3 or 6 months) only changes the three period figures: Available is always today's balance, regardless of the filter.
home.where: This is where everything you record lands: recurring products under “Upcoming fixed expenses”, goals and debts with their progress bars, expenses split by category, and warnings when you spend more than you earn or a debt goes past due.

accounts.hook: Where your money sits: bank, cash, foreign currency.
accounts.what: Each account is a place where you keep money, with its own currency. Its balance is never typed in: it comes from your transactions, and shows in three parts — total, reserved (locked by goals) and available.
accounts.form: Name, type, bank and currency. The currency is not a detail: it defines the currency every transaction on that account is recorded in, and it can't be mixed within one account.
accounts.where: This is the first thing to create: without an account you can't record transactions, close a purchase or contribute to a goal. Its balance feeds the Available figure on Home.

transactions.hook: The ledger: every income and every expense.
transactions.what: The record of everything coming in and going out. Each entry stores the rate of the day it happened, so past entries don't change value when the dollar moves.
transactions.form: The first thing is the type: income, expense, debt payment or debt collection. The fields change with it. Income and expenses ask for amount, category, store if it was a purchase, the account, a description and the date. A debt payment or collection asks for none of that: just which debt it goes to and whether it is a partial payment or settles it in full. If bolívars are involved you pick the rate: BCV (the default), Parallel or Manual.
transactions.where: It feeds the Income, Expenses and Net figures on Home, the expenses-by-category chart, and the balance of the account you used.

categories.hook: So you can tell where the money goes.
categories.what: Income or expense labels. Each one only works for its own type: an expense category never shows up when you record income.
categories.form: Name and type. That's it — the point is to keep few and clear ones.
categories.where: When recording a transaction, in the “Expenses by category” chart on Home, and as a product's default category: that's what lets a closed cart classify itself.

products.hook: Your catalogue: what you buy and what you pay monthly.
products.what: The things you buy often. They serve two separate purposes: building your grocery cart, and keeping the price history of each item.
products.form: Name, unit and default category. Marking it as a staple says “I always buy this”, and “every how many days” is what lets the app know when it's due for a restock. If it's instead a service you pay every month (power, internet), set the recurrence and its day.
products.where: In the cart: picking it suggests its last price, and the “Add what's missing” button pulls in the staples that are already due. Recurring ones show up under “Upcoming fixed expenses” on Home. And each product page has a chart of how its price moved.

stores.hook: Where you shop, so you can compare prices.
stores.what: The list of supermarkets and shops where you buy.
stores.where: When creating a cart, when recording an expense, and in the price history: since every price is stored with its store, over time you can see where each product is cheaper.

shopping.hook: The cart with a budget, to take to the supermarket.
shopping.what: A shopping list with a budget you use inside the store: tick off what goes into the cart and type the real price, and the bar warns you when you're going over.
shopping.form: When creating the cart: name, store and budget. Inside, each item can be a product from your catalogue (which brings its last price as an estimate, in grey, for you to correct) or a one-off name.
shopping.where: Closing the purchase turns it into a real expense: a single transaction with the total, the account you paid with, and the heaviest category among the products. It also stores each product's price, which is what feeds next time's estimates.

debts.hook: What you owe and what you're owed, with part payments.
debts.what: Debts in both directions. Each part payment reduces the outstanding balance until it's settled.
debts.form: Who it's with, how much, in which currency, whether you owe it or you're owed it, and the due date if there is one.
debts.where: On Home, with its paid-over-total bar, and as a warning when a debt of yours goes past due. Note: recording a debt or a payment does not move any account balance — if the money actually left an account, record it as a transaction too.

goals.hook: Save for something without taking it out of the account.
goals.what: A goal reserves money inside an account. What's reserved doesn't leave your net worth, but it stops counting as available, so you don't spend it without noticing.
goals.form: Name, the account where it's reserved, the target amount, the currency and a target date if you want one.
goals.where: On Home with its progress bar, and in the account balance: every contribution lowers Available even though the account total stays the same.
